ops.html: Fix GitHub issue #235: avoid redundant install+test+build in CI
ops.src: # Fix GitHub issue #235: avoid redundant install+test+build in CI

ops.html: Context
ops.src: ## Context

ops.html: Issue #235 ("improve the CI workflow"): the Crypto1 test suite is slow, and .github/workflows/ci.yml currently runs the full yarn install → yarn test:ci → yarn build sequence twice on every push to master — once in the test job, and again from scratch in the deploy job (which needs dist/ for the GitHub Pages deploy + npm publish, and needs coverage output for the Coveralls upload). The fix requested: build/test once in the test job, upload the results as a GitHub Actions artifact, and have deploy download and reuse them instead of rebuilding.
ops.src: [Issue #235](https://github.com/taichunmin/chameleon-ultra.js/issues/235) ("improve the CI workflow"): the `Crypto1` test suite is slow, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` currently runs the full `yarn` install → `yarn test:ci` → `yarn build` sequence **twice** on every push to `master` — once in the `test` job, and again from scratch in the `deploy` job (which needs `dist/` for the GitHub Pages deploy + npm publish, and needs coverage output for the Coveralls upload). The fix requested: build/test once in the `test` job, upload the results as a GitHub Actions artifact, and have `deploy` download and reuse them instead of rebuilding.

ops.html: After the plan above was implemented and pushed, the test job failed at the actions/setup-node@v7 step:
ops.src: After the plan above was implemented and pushed, the `test` job failed at the `actions/setup-node@v7` step:

ops.html:
error Error: Failed to replace env in config: ${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}
    at NpmRegistry.normalizeConfig (.../yarn/lib/cli.js:31940:69)
ops.src:
```
error Error: Failed to replace env in config: ${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}
    at NpmRegistry.normalizeConfig (.../yarn/lib/cli.js:31940:69)
```

ops.html: Root cause: actions/setup-node's registry-url input always writes an .npmrc containing //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}. Yarn Classic (v1.22.22) eagerly evaluates that config for any yarn invocation — including the internal yarn cache dir probe setup-node runs to resolve its cache path when cache: yarn is set — and throws if NODE_AUTH_TOKEN isn't set. Nothing in this repo's CI ever set that env var, since publishing goes through JS-DevTools/npm-publish's OIDC trusted publishing, not npm/yarn publish directly.
ops.src: **Root cause:** `actions/setup-node`'s `registry-url` input always writes an `.npmrc` containing `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. Yarn Classic (v1.22.22) eagerly evaluates that config for *any* yarn invocation — including the internal `yarn cache dir` probe `setup-node` runs to resolve its cache path when `cache: yarn` is set — and throws if `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` isn't set. Nothing in this repo's CI ever set that env var, since publishing goes through `JS-DevTools/npm-publish`'s OIDC trusted publishing, not `npm`/`yarn publish` directly.

ops.html: Fix 2 — deploy job still needs some pinned Node/npm, for a different reason: while investigating, confirmed by reading JS-DevTools/npm-publish's source (src/npm/call-npm-cli.ts, src/npm/use-npm-environment.ts) that it does not implement publish via raw HTTP — it shells out to the system npm CLI via child_process.spawn, using its own scoped temp .npmrc (which is why it doesn't touch ~/.npmrc). Its README states OIDC trusted publishing requires npm ≥11.5.1. With setup-node entirely removed from deploy (per the original plan, since none of its other steps are Node-based actions), that job would depend on whatever npm version happens to be pre-baked into the ubuntu-latest runner image — unpinned and not guaranteed to meet that minimum.

Its README states OIDC trusted publishing requires **npm ≥11.5.1**. With `setup-node` entirely removed from `deploy` (per the original plan, since none of its other steps are Node-based actions), that job would depend on whatever `npm` version happens to be pre-baked into the `ubuntu-latest` runner image — unpinned and not guaranteed to meet that minimum.

ops.html: Fix 3 — Coveralls had "nothing to report": confirmed via Vitest's own docs (Context7) that coverage.reporter defaults to ['text', 'html', 'clover', 'json'] — no lcov — so coverage/lcov.info was never generated in the first place, regardless of the CI restructuring. coverallsapp/github-action@v2 looks for ./coverage/lcov.info by default and had genuinely nothing to find. This was a pre-existing gap, just newly surfaced now that the pipeline actually depends on that file flowing correctly through the build-output artifact.

This was a pre-existing gap, just newly surfaced now that the pipeline actually depends on that file flowing correctly through the `build-output` artifact.

Passing --coverage.reporter via CLI replaces the config default array rather than merging with it, so text is re-added explicitly alongside lcov to keep a readable summary in the CI job log.)

ops.html: Also made the coverage provider explicit (--coverage.provider=v8) — confirmed via Vitest docs that v8 is already the default and matches the @vitest/coverage-v8 package already installed (not -istanbul), so this is a no-op today, just documentation-as-config against future default changes.

ops.html: Note: per Vitest's own CLI docs, the bare --coverage flag is not redundant alongside --coverage.provider=/--coverage.reporter= — dot-notation options configure nested settings but do not themselves flip coverage.enabled to true ("Remember to always include --coverage.enabled when using dot notation for coverage options"). --coverage is the one doing that; the dotted flags only apply once coverage is already enabled.
ops.src: Note: per Vitest's own CLI docs, the bare `--coverage` flag is *not* redundant alongside `--coverage.provider=`/`--coverage.reporter=` — dot-notation options configure nested settings but do not themselves flip `coverage.enabled` to `true` ("Remember to always include `--coverage.enabled` when using dot notation for coverage options"). `--coverage` is the one doing that; the dotted flags only apply once coverage is already enabled.

ops.html: Fix 4 (supersedes Fix 3's root-cause theory) — the real reason Coveralls had "nothing to report"
ops.src: ## Fix 4 (supersedes Fix 3's root-cause theory) — the real reason Coveralls had "nothing to report"

ops.html: Fix 3 turned out to be treating a symptom, not the actual cause. The real bug: package.json's "test": "vitest -r ./src --testTimeout 180000" sets Vitest's root to ./src, and coverage.reportsDirectory (default './coverage') resolves relative to that root — so coverage output has always landed at src/coverage/, not <repo-root>/coverage/. Confirmed two ways:
ops.src: Fix 3 turned out to be treating a symptom, not the actual cause. The real bug: `package.json`'s `"test": "vitest -r ./src --testTimeout 180000"` sets Vitest's `root` to `./src`, and `coverage.reportsDirectory` (default `'./coverage'`) resolves **relative to that root** — so coverage output has always landed at `src/coverage/`, not `<repo-root>/coverage/`. Confirmed two ways:

ops.html: 1. Reproduced locally: yarn vitest -r ./src run src/helper.test.ts --coverage ... → ./src/coverage/lcov.info, not ./coverage/lcov.info.
ops.src: 1. Reproduced locally: `yarn vitest -r ./src run src/helper.test.ts --coverage ...` → `./src/coverage/lcov.info`, not `./coverage/lcov.info`.

ops.html: 1. The pre-PR (working) CI log literally shows Detected coverage file: src/coverage/clover.xml.
ops.src: 2. The pre-PR (working) CI log literally shows `Detected coverage file: src/coverage/clover.xml`.

ops.html: This means Vitest's default reporters (clover included) were already producing a Coveralls-supported format (confirmed: Clover XML is in coverallsapp/coverage-reporter's supported-formats list) at src/coverage/ all along — Fix 3's lcov reporter addition wasn't the missing ingredient. The actual bug was in ci.yml's Upload build output step: it captured coverage/ (repo-root-relative), which never matched anything, so the coverage report silently never made it into the artifact (upload-artifact's default if-no-files-found: warn doesn't fail the step). deploy then had nothing to find, since it no longer re-runs the test suite itself (that's the point of this whole fix). Pre-PR this was masked because deploy generated src/coverage/ fresh, in its own job, immediately before the Coveralls step ran — no cross-job hand-off was ever involved.
ops.src: This means Vitest's default reporters (`clover` included) were already producing a Coveralls-supported format (confirmed: Clover XML is in `coverallsapp/coverage-reporter`'s supported-formats list) at `src/coverage/` all along — Fix 3's `lcov` reporter addition wasn't the missing ingredient. The actual bug was in `ci.yml`'s `Upload build output` step: it captured `coverage/` (repo-root-relative), which never matched anything, so the coverage report silently never made it into the artifact (`upload-artifact`'s default `if-no-files-found: warn` doesn't fail the step). `deploy` then had nothing to find, since it no longer re-runs the test suite itself (that's the point of this whole fix).
